rv.q: It is rare for a family show to be both funny and spine-tinglingly creepy, but an achievement playwright Lewis Hetherington pulls off in his imaginative reworking of the 18th-century fable.
If a thing is worth waiting for, then Beauty and the Beast was it.
This show is an entertaining, if uneven affair, a freewheeling twist on a famous fairytale that veers disorientatingly between thoughtful drama and chaotic pantomime.
The Citizens Theatre’s Beauty and the Beast is a festive fairytale that gleefully sidesteps pantomime cliché, offering Glasgow audiences a darker, roguish, and heartwarming spectacle.
Indeed, it was the apt introduction to a rollicking festive farce with a Citz twist.

cn.t: Critics praise this imaginative, spine-tinglingly creepy yet funny reworking of the classic fairytale that strips away Disney sentimentality, with the narrative's certainty and macabre edge making for entertaining festive fare at the Citizens Theatre.
